name: Achenkirch
kurzbeschreibung: Relaxation spot on the northern shore of the Achensee, featuring the Christlum ski area and lakeside access.
beschreibung:
Overview

Achenkirch is situated at an elevation of 916 meters on the northern shore of Lake Achensee, Tyrol's largest body of water with an area of 6.8 square kilometers and depths up to 133 meters, often hailed as the 'Tyrolean Fjord'. Located in the district of Schwaz, the municipality extends across approximately 114 square kilometers in the northern Achental valley, framed by the Karwendel Mountains to the west and the Rofan Range to the east. Reaching north to the Bavarian border at Achen Pass, Achenkirch is home to around 2,250 residents across several hamlets including Achenwald, Klausen, and the historic ferry terminal Scholastika, offering a year-round paradise for alpine recreation.

History

Settlement in the valley dates to the 12th century: around 1140, the Lords of Schlitters donated the lakeside area, then referred to as Emmaus, to the Benedictine monastery of Saint Georgenberg-Fiecht. Until 1971, the municipality was officially known as Achental before being renamed Achenkirch after its parish church of Saint John the Baptist. For centuries, the valley was a vital trade and salt route connecting Hall in Tirol with Bavaria. The lakeside staging point Scholastika served as an indispensable customs house, boat landing, and coaching inn. The region's rich rural heritage is showcased in the Sixenhof Heritage Museum, an authentic Tyrolean farmstead dating back to 1383.

Getting There

By car from Innsbruck, take the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wiesing/Achensee exit, then continue north along the B181 lake road to Achenkirch (roughly 45 kilometers, 40 minutes). From Munich, motorists can travel toll-free via Tegernsee and the Achen Pass on route B307 directly into town. By rail, Jenbach station in the Inn Valley provides mainline train connections, where VVT regional bus line 4080 connects travelers to Achenkirch every half hour. Seasonally from May to October, the historic Achensee Railway, Europe's oldest steam rack-and-pinion line dating from 1889, climbs from Jenbach to Seespitz, connecting to passenger steamboats bound for Scholastika.

Tips

Winter sports enthusiasts head to the Christlum ski area (950 to 1,800 m), featuring 27 kilometers of slopes and a floodlit natural toboggan run. In summer, Lake Achensee's thermal breezes create premier conditions for windsurfing, kitesurfing, and sailing. The scenic Mariensteig lakeside trail winds along sheer cliffs to the rustic Gaisalm, Tyrol's only alpine inn accessible solely on foot or by passenger boat. Experienced mountaineers can summit the Seekarspitze (2,053 m) for striking panoramic vistas over the turquoise waters. The Sixenhof Heritage Museum offers compelling exhibits on traditional rural crafts and lake navigation.
